Playbook.name: AD/Windows — Security Event Log Cleared - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: The Windows Security event log was cleared (1102). Triage question: is this an attacker destroying evidence after an intrusion, or a sanctioned maintenance/reimage action?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Clearing the Security log removes the primary record of authentication and privilege activity - a classic post-exploitation anti-forensics step.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host whose Security log was cleared.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Reimaging/decommission clears logs legitimately; an interactive clear on a production server by a non-admin, or right after suspicious activity, is anti-forensics.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the log clear is sanctioned maintenance or evidence destruction following intrusion activity.

Step.name: Confirm the clear event and actor
Step.Purpose: Identify who cleared the log on which host and whether multiple hosts were cleared (broad anti-forensics).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "1102" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.SubjectDomainName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: One host by a known admin during a maintenance window = likely benign. Several hosts cleared close together, or a non-admin actor, = anti-forensics.

Step.name: What happened on this host just before the clear
Step.Purpose: Suspicious activity (new admin logon, service install, privilege use) shortly BEFORE the clear is what the attacker is trying to erase.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4624","4672","4688","7045","4720","4728") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY winlog.event_data.LogonType | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A new interactive/RDP logon then service install then log clear is a textbook intrusion sequence. Quiet history before a maintenance clear supports benign.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows suspicious activity (new privileged logon, service/account creation) shortly before the clear, or INV-01 shows multiple hosts cleared.
INV-01 shows a non-admin or unexpected principal clearing a production host's log with no maintenance record.
INV-01 shows a known admin clearing during a documented reimage/maintenance window.
Actor is an admin but no maintenance record and no clear preceding activity.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-CLEAR-EVENT, INV-02-CLEAR-PRECEDING to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Sanctioned maintenance, reimaging, or decommissioning that clears logs.

Indicators.Item: Quiet, normal history before the clear.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the maintenance record; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Evidence destruction to cover intrusion activity.

Indicators.Item: Suspicious privileged activity immediately before the clear.
Non-admin or compromised account performing it.

SOCAction.Item: Preserve remaining/forwarded logs; treat the host as compromised and isolate.
Reconstruct from forwarded/SIEM copies; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured job or tool clearing logs unintentionally.

Indicators.Item: An automation account clearing per a broken maintenance script.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the job; ensure logs forward before any clear.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Preserve forwarded copies; isolate the host if intrusion indicators exist.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Full host forensics; reconstruct the cleared window from SIEM; hunt lateral movement.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Ensure real-time log forwarding so local clears do not lose evidence; restrict who can clear logs.

QualityChecks.Check: SIEM already holds forwarded copies - the clear does not blind the investigation, it IS the signal.
Companion rule 'Windows - Event Log Cleared (All Channels)' covers 1102/104 across channels.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Maintenance record verified; no preceding suspicious activity.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host forensics complete; intrusion scope reconstructed from SIEM; eradication done.
